why.quote: The requirements for the Minor in Mathematics consists of four lower-division and five upper-division courses: ... Math 51 (formerly 1A): Calculus I ... Math 52 (formerly 1B): Calculus II ... Math 53: Multivariable Calculus ... Math 54: Linear Algebra and Differential Equations or Math 56 Linear Algebra*
why.reasoning: The catalog rules have no lower-division block, but the department lists four required lower-division courses. The major-specific substitutions for Math 54 (Physics 89 for Physics majors; EECS 16A+16B for CS/EECS majors) are left out because GradTrak can't condition on the student's major; they are noted in the log.

why.quote: One additional upper-division mathematics course, or a non-Math upper-division class from the pre-approved list of Applied Mathematics electives.
why.reasoning: The catalog requires 3 courses from a non-Math list. The department requires only one elective (5 upper-division courses = 4 required + 1), and that elective may be any upper-division Math course. The catalog's non-Math list is kept unchanged: the linked Applied Math page only shows 'sample clusters' rather than a definitive pre-approved list, so it gives no explicit basis for changing it.

notStated: Which non-Math courses are on the definitive 'pre-approved list of Applied Mathematics electives': the linked page (https://math.berkeley.edu/undergraduate/major/applied) shows only sample clusters, which differ from the catalog list (e.g. it includes COMPSCI C100, COMPSCI 176, ECON 103, MCB 160/166, STAT 133/140/151B/156 and omits COMPSCI 162/164/170, ELENG 120/122/123, EPS 121).
Whether honors versions (MATH H104, H110, H113, H185) are accepted for the core; the catalog accepts them and the department page doesn't say.
